en.title: Democrats Win Control of Congress as Trump Faces Cabinet and Diplomatic Fallout
en.dek: Democrats cleared 250 House seats and won control of both chambers, while Trump addressed Russia, Iran, and tech stocks.
facts: Democrats cleared 250 House seats and won control of both chambers of Congress, according to The New York Times and DW.
The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on November 5 as investors reacted to possible tighter AI scrutiny, according to Nikkei Asia.
Trump met Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington and said a Russia-Ukraine deal is near, according to Al Jazeera.
Trump told reporters he would rather not destroy the rest of Iran but maybe he will have to, according to The Jerusalem Post.
Vice President J.D. Vance criticized the Trump administration after the midterm defeat, according to SRF.
The White House denied that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth plan to leave, according to BBC.
body: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. The New York Times reported that Democrats cleared 250 House seats. The Straits Times and DW reported that the party won control of both chambers.

President Donald Trump met Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington. Trump said a "big, beautiful agreement" was coming, according to The Kyiv Independent. Al Jazeera reported that Trump said a Russia-Ukraine deal is near after the meeting.

Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that he would rather not destroy the rest of Iran but maybe he will have to, according to The Jerusalem Post. Euronews reported that US officials warned Gulf allies to prepare for possible new strikes.
Vice President J.D. Vance posted online after the Republican midterm defeat and criticized the Trump administration, according to SRF. ZDF reported that Vance sought distance from the government.

The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on November 5, according to Nikkei Asia. BBC reported that global tech stocks plunged as investors reacted to possible tighter scrutiny of the AI industry and data center construction.

The White House denied that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth plan to leave their jobs after Republican election losses, according to BBC. Rubio also denied plans to leave his post for a White House bid, The Japan Times reported.
The 2026 U.S. midterm elections produced Republican losses and a shift in congressional control. DW reported that the GOP was reeling after losing both houses of Congress.
